holidays.name: National Apple Turnover Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the flaky, golden pastry pocket stuffed with gooey spiced apples. Bakeries and dessert lovers mark it by indulging in a warm turnover, ideally with a scoop of ice cream on the side.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it is an unofficial observance that grew out of food-industry promotion and social media. The turnover itself traces back to European pastry traditions, where fruit-filled folded dough was a popular portable treat.
holidays.funFact: The word 'turnover' comes from the way the dough is turned over to enclose the filling, which makes it one of the few pastries named after its assembly instructions.

holidays.name: National Bikini Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the iconic two-piece swimsuit, celebrated with beach outings, pool parties, and a lot of fashion nostalgia.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the debut of the modern bikini on July 5, 1946, when French engineer Louis Réard unveiled it at a Paris swimming pool. He named it after Bikini Atoll, where the US had just conducted atomic bomb tests, hoping the swimsuit would cause an explosive reaction.
holidays.funFact: No professional model would wear Réard's design because it was considered too scandalous, so he hired Micheline Bernardini, a nude dancer from the Casino de Paris, to model it.

holidays.name: National Graham Cracker Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble honey-sweet cracker that makes s'mores, cheesecake crusts, and nostalgic snack-time memories possible.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance honoring the cracker created by Presbyterian minister Sylvester Graham in the 1820s–1830s as part of a health reform movement.
holidays.funFact: Sylvester Graham believed bland whole-grain foods would curb 'unhealthy impulses,' so the original graham cracker was meant to be dull on purpose, which is the opposite of today's sugary versions.

holidays.name: Workaholics Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day that encourages people who live for their jobs to take a breath, step away from their desks, and remember that life exists outside the office.
holidays.origin: An unofficial awareness day that gets observed in the days following a major holiday, when many people are tempted to sneak back into work mode. It is meant to raise awareness about work-life balance and burnout.
holidays.funFact: The word 'workaholic' was coined in 1968 by the American minister and writer Wayne Oates, who based it on the word 'alcoholic' to describe his own compulsion to work.

holidays.name: Independence Day of Venezuela
holidays.description: Venezuelans celebrate with military parades, flags, music, and gatherings honoring the country's break from Spanish colonial rule.
holidays.origin: On July 5, 1811, Venezuela's congress formally declared independence from Spain, making it one of the first Latin American countries to do so.
holidays.funFact: Venezuela's declaration came nearly a decade before most of its neighbors, and the country's name means 'Little Venice,' given by explorers who saw stilt houses over Lake Maracaibo.
